results.title: What is HIL Testing in Automotive? | Efficient Prototyping & Real-Time Results | Safer Vehicle Development | OPAL-RT
results.content: # What is HIL testing in automotive? Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing is a proven method that drives faster innovation and stronger reliability in automotive projects. HIL testing provides a way to connect real components to simulated ones, allowing you to spot issues earlier in the development lifecycle. HIL testing meets that need by combining dynamic virtual models with actual control units, capturing real sensor data, and feeding it back through real-time processors. ## What is HIL testing in automotive? HIL testing in the automotive domain refers to a validation process that ties physical hardware components, such as electronic control units (ECUs), to sophisticated software simulations. What is HIL in automotive can be described as a technique that isolates specific modules for deeper testing, which saves resources and tackles the complexities associated with modern vehicle electronics. ## Benefits of HIL testing in the automotive domain. HIL testing in the automotive domain answers these priorities through a controlled, repeatable simulation that offers valuable insights. * **Accelerated validation:** HIL setups allow you to test multiple conditions at any stage, cutting extended lab or road sessions. HIL testing replicates real load conditions for each control signal, helping you verify functionality without risking wear on physical components. HIL setups facilitate closed-loop testing of sensors like radar, lidar, and cameras by simulating the data they would produce. HIL testing empowers teams to simulate varied voltage and temperature profiles, revealing any flaws before a battery pack is installed. HIL testing integrates actual controllers with simulated vehicle models, creating a more accurate replication of operating conditions. ### Why focus on HIL testing in the automotive domain? HIL in automotive is a technique linking real components (often ECUs) to digital simulations for testing. ### Does HIL testing help with cost-effectiveness? ### Can HIL testing handle evolving vehicle software updates? Hardware in the loop testing for power electronics helps your team validate controllers earlier, study demanding grid and fault conditions safely, and build a reliable path from models to high-confidence hardware results. Real-time HIL and SIL simulation turn renewable integration projects into faster, safer efforts by validating control strategies and grid interactions in the lab before deployment.

results.title: (PDF) Platoon Priority Visualization Modeling and Optimization for Signal Coordination in Connected Vehicle Environment
results.content: Although connected vehicle (CV)-based signal coordination has some proposed prototypes and has been investigated by several different strategies, the existing works have issues that require attention, including additional CV-based system uncertainties and platoon priority request considerations. Thus, a generalized framework consisting of a platoon-based bicyclic coordination diagram (Bi-PCD), a new probabilistic surrogate quantification, and a platoon priority-based offset optimization in the CV environment is proposed to improve the coordination performance. The comprehensive analysis showed that the proposed Bi-PCD and the platoon priority-based offset optimization could further improve performances of the signal coordination. Platoon-based bicyclic coordination diagram modeling in a CV environment: (a) time-space diagram and the corresponding control scheme, (b) single bicyclic coordination diagram for adjacent two consecutive cycles C1 and C2, and (c) an illustrative Bi-PCD with several cycles. Thus, CV-based signal coordination systems offer huge potential utilizing the real-time spatial and temporal data advantage when addressing many traffic-related issues, and accordingly, have shown promising benefits to performance over the existing typical signal control systems [1,5]. Consequently, many CV-based signal coordination approaches have been introduced in the past decade from both offline offset optimization using large trajectory data and online control utilizing the real-time CV data perspectives [8]. The emerging CV technology provides two potential benefits for signal control systems, which are fine-grained spatial and temporal vehicle and infrastructure data, and real-time data transmission via high-frequency vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication [1,5]. Targeting at resolving these issues, this work proposes a real-time predictive coordination method consisting of a probabilistic single-vehicle-based dynamic platoon dispersion model, an extended link performance function, and a real-time model predictive control (MPC)-based coordination framework. [99] proposed a method to utilize CV-based trajectory data to assess signal coordination quality, thus optimizing the traffic signals. Specifically, we incorporated loop detector and CV data into an adaptive signal controller and measured several mobility- and event-based performance metrics under different degrees of traffic observability (i.e., detector-only, CV-only, and CV and loop detector data) with various CV market penetration rates. At the same market penetration rate, signal control with CV-only data resulted in the same traffic performance, progression quality, and travel time reliability as the signal control with CV and loop detector data.
